40202-the-annals-of-ann.title: The Annals Of Ann
40202-the-annals-of-ann.creator: Unknown
40202-the-annals-of-ann.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Maybe some rainy day, a hundred years from now, a little girl will find this book in the attic, all covered with dust, and will sit down and read it, while the rain sounds soft and pattery on the outside, and her mother calls and calls without getting an answer. This is not at all the right way to do, but what can they expect of you when your attic is such a very delicious place?

arxiv-1708-04383.title: Constrained Path Monte Carlo method for spin 1 / 2 1/2 fermions at unitarity limit
arxiv-1708-04383.creator: F. Etminan, M. M. Firoozabadi
arxiv-1708-04383.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by F. Etminan, M. M. Firoozabadi. We present calculations for spin 1 / 2 1/2 fermions at unitarity limit, where the effective range of the interaction is zero and the scattering length is infinite. We compute the ground-state energy for a system of 6, 10,14,18 and 20 particles, with equal numbers of up and down spins in a periodic cube in the full ground-state constrained-path Monte Carlo (CPMC) method using the extended, attractive Hubbard model.

arxiv-2209-02973.title: Foundations of probability-raising causality in Markov decision processes Thanks: This work was funded by DFG grant 389792660 as part of TRR 248 – CPEC (see https://perspicuous-computing.science , the Cluster of Excellence EXC 2050/1 (CeTI, project ID 390696704, as part of Germany’s Excellence Strat
arxiv-2209-02973.creator: Christel Baier ORCID:0000-0002-5321-9343, Jakob Piribauer ORCID:0000-0003-4829-0476, Robin Ziemek ORCID:0000-0002-8490-1433
arxiv-2209-02973.description: Abstract . This work introduces a novel cause-effect relation in Markov decision processes using the probability-raising principle. Initially, sets of states as causes and effects are considered, which is subsequently extended to regular path properties as effects and then as causes. The paper lays the mathematical foundations and analyzes the algorithmic properties of these cause-effect relations.

arxiv-2305-10276.title: Chain-of-Symbol Prompting for Spatial Reasoning in Large Language Models
arxiv-2305-10276.creator: Hanxu Hu, Hongyuan Lu, Huajian Zhang, Yun-Ze Song, Wai Lam, Yue Zhang
arxiv-2305-10276.description: Abstract In this paper, we first investigate the performance of LLMs on complex planning tasks that require LLMs to understand a virtual spatial environment simulated via natural language and act or reason correspondingly in text. By evaluating on classic spatial planning scenarios, we found that current LLMs still lack abilities to handle spatial relationships in texts.

arxiv-2312-00398.title: Learning to Estimate Critical Gait Parameters from Single-View RGB Videos with Transformer-Based Attention Network
arxiv-2312-00398.creator: Hung Le, Hieu Pham
arxiv-2312-00398.description: Abstract Musculoskeletal diseases and cognitive impairments in patients lead to difficulties in movement as well as negative effects on their psychological health. Clinical gait analysis, a vital tool for early diagnosis and treatment, traditionally relies on expensive optical motion capture systems. Recent advances in computer vision and deep learning have opened the door to more accessible and cost-effective alternatives.

arxiv-2401-05677.title: On the discrete analogues of Appell function F 1 F_{1}
arxiv-2401-05677.creator: Ravi Dwivedi, Vivek Sahai
arxiv-2401-05677.description: Abstract In the present paper, two discrete forms of Appell function F 1 F_{1} are introduced and studied. We examine the first discrete form in detail and give the results directly for the second. We study their regions of convergence, differential properties, integral representations, recursion relations, finite and infinite sums.

arxiv-2407-07251.title: R. A. Fisher’s Exact Test Revisited
arxiv-2407-07251.creator: Martin Mugnier
arxiv-2407-07251.description: Abstract This note provides a conceptual clarification of Ronald Aylmer Fisher’s (1935) pioneering exact test in the context of the Lady Testing Tea experiment. It unveils a critical implicit assumption in Fisher’s calibration: the taster minimizes expected misclassification given fixed probabilistic information.

arxiv-2412-04623.title: Using Diffusion Priors for Video Amodal Segmentation
arxiv-2412-04623.creator: Kaihua Chen, Deva Ramanan, Tarasha Khurana
arxiv-2412-04623.description: Abstract Object permanence in humans is a fundamental cue that helps in understanding persistence of objects, even when they are fully occluded in the scene. Present day methods in object segmentation do not account for this amodal nature of the world, and only work for segmentation of visible or modal objects.

arxiv-2502-15775.title: Serverless Edge Computing: A Taxonomy, Systematic Literature Review, Current Trends and Research Challenges
arxiv-2502-15775.creator: Iqra Batool, Sania Kanwal
arxiv-2502-15775.description: Abstract In recent years, the rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) nodes and devices has seamlessly integrated technology into everyday life, amplifying the demand for optimized computing solutions. To meet the critical Quality of Service (QoS) requirements—such as reduced latency, efficient bandwidth usage, swift reaction times, scalability, privacy, and security—serverless edge computing has emerged as a transformative paradigm.

arxiv-2512-10339.title: On the Collapse of Generative Paths: A Criterion and Correction for Diffusion Steering
arxiv-2512-10339.creator:
ame Ziseok Lee, 
ame Minyeong Hwang, 
ame Sanghyun Jo, 
ame Wooyeol Lee, 
ame Jihyung Ko, 
ame Young Bin Park, 
ame Jae-Mun Choi, 
ame Eunho Yang, 
ame Kyungsu Kim
arxiv-2512-10339.description: Abstract Inference-time steering enables pretrained diffusion/flow models to be adapted to new tasks without retraining. A widely used approach is the ratio-of-densities method, which defines a time-indexed target path by reweighting probability-density trajectories from multiple models with positive, or in some cases, negative exponents.

arxiv-2601-18732.title: Optimal Use of Preferences in Artificial Intelligence Algorithms
arxiv-2601-18732.creator: Joshua S. Gans
arxiv-2601-18732.description: Abstract Machine learning systems embed preferences either in training losses or through post-processing of calibrated predictions. Applying information design methods from Strack and Yang (2024), this paper provides decision-problem-agnostic conditions under which separation—training preference-free and applying preferences ex post is optimal. Unlike prior work that requires specifying downstream objectives, the welfare results here apply uniformly across decision problems.

pmc-10613466.creator: Yingshuo Sun, Ting Gong, Dongdong Wu, Yongzhi Feng, Qi Gao, Jiabao Xing, Xiaoyu Zheng, Zebu Song, Xing Liu, Xiongnan Chen, Yankuo Sun, Guihong Zhang, Lang Gong
pmc-10613466.description: Porcine epidemic diarrhea (PED) is an enterophilic infectious disease caused by the porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV), which can lead to dehydration-like diarrhea in piglets with a mortality rate of up to 100%, causing huge economic losses to the global pig industry.

pmc-10741141.title: Characterization of Inflammasomes and Their Regulation in the Red Fox
pmc-10741141.creator: Huijeong Ahn, Dong-Hyuk Jeong, Gilyoung Lee, Suk-Jin Lee, Jeong-Jin Yang, Yo-Han Kim, Tae-Wook Hahn, Sooyoung Choi, Geun-Shik Lee, Brian L Cypher
pmc-10741141.description: Simple SummaryStudying inflammasomes in red foxes is crucial for wildlife veterinary medicine, as it helps in treating and preventing inflammatory diseases in foxes. Inflammasomes, protein complexes in innate immune cells, regulate the release of interleukin (IL)-1β, a pro-inflammatory cytokine, in response to cytosolic danger signals, such as pathogens.

pmc-10748634.title: Evaluating the Utility of Plain Radiograph and Computerised Tomography Scanning in Identifying Concomitant Foot Fractures in Patients with Unstable Lisfranc Injuries
pmc-10748634.creator: Junaid Aamir, Robyn Caldwell, Dileep Karthikappallil, Mamdouh M Elbannan, Hiro Tanaka, Lyndon W Mason
pmc-10748634.description: Category:Midfoot/Forefoot; TraumaIntroduction/Purpose:Lisfranc fracture dislocations are uncommon injuries, which frequently require surgical intervention. Currently, there is varying evidence on the diagnostic utility of plain radiographs (XR) and CT in identifying Lisfranc injuries and concomitant fractures. Our aim was to identify the utility of XR as compared to CT, with the nul hypothesis that there was no difference in fracture identification.

pmc-11436914.title: Dataset from a human-in-the-loop approach to identify functionally important protein residues from literature
pmc-11436914.creator: Melanie Vollmar, Santosh Tirunagari, Deborah Harrus, David Armstrong, Romana Gáborová, Deepti Gupta, Marcelo Querino Lima Afonso, Genevieve Evans, Sameer Velankar
pmc-11436914.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We present a novel system that leverages curators in the loop to develop a dataset and model for detecting structure features and functional annotations at residue-level from standard publication text. Our approach involves the integration of data from multiple resources, including PDBe, EuropePMC, PubMedCentral, and PubMed, combined with annotation guidelines from UniProt, and LitSuggest and HuggingFace models as tools in the annotation process.

pmc-11541155.title: Patient Perspectives on Blended Internet-Based and Face-to-Face Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Alcohol Use Disorder: Qualitative Study
pmc-11541155.creator: Kristine Tarp, Regina Christiansen, Randi Bilberg, Simone Borkner, Caroline Dalsgaard, Marie Paldam Folker, Anette Søgaard Nielsen
pmc-11541155.description: BackgroundHarmful alcohol consumption has been identified as a major contributor to disease, mortality, and social harm, accounting for 5.3% of worldwide deaths annually. In Denmark, an estimated 150,000 people suffer from alcohol use disorder (AUD), but a low proportion seek treatment due to person- and treatment-related barriers.

pmc-11592843.title: Molecular Mechanisms Responsible for Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Dependent Attenuation of Tear Hyperosmolarity and Immune Cell-Driven Inflammation in the Eyes of Patients with Dry Eye Disease
pmc-11592843.creator: Carl Randall Harrell, Valentin Djonov, Ana Volarevic, Aleksandar Arsenijevic, Vladislav Volarevic
pmc-11592843.description: Background: Dry eye disease (DED) is a chronic condition characterized by a decrease in tear production or an increase in tear evaporation, leading to inflammation and damage of the ocular surface. Dysfunction of ion channels, tear hyperosmolarity and immune cell-driven inflammation create a vicious circle responsible for the pathological changes in the eyes of DED patients.

pmc-11633058.title: Psychological interventions for improvement of symptoms of post-stroke depression – study protocol of the depression-intervention study for optimization of reconvalesence after stroke (DISCOVER)
pmc-11633058.creator: Lino Braadt, Simone Fischer, Markus Naumann, Philipp Zickler, Thomas Schneider-Axmann, Laura Mühlich, Katharina Körber, Alexander Lassner, Wolfgang Strube, Astrid Röh, Alkomiet Hasan, Michael Ertl
pmc-11633058.description: IntroductionBesides functional outcomes, mental health and health-related quality of life (HRQoL) are significant measures in chronic diseases, such as stroke. Post-stroke depression (PSD) is an important complication affecting up to one in three stroke survivors. So far, specific programs to screen, detect and treat these patients are lacking but might be a crucial component in stroke aftercare.

pmc-13037003.title: CCL chemokines as prognostic and immunotherapeutic markers in prostate cancer: a comprehensive analysis
pmc-13037003.creator: Yao Bai, Chaojin Liang, Jie Gu, LuoWu Wang, Ke Yang
pmc-13037003.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to delineate the prognostic significance of CCL family expression in Prostate Cancer (PCa) and explore their immunomodulatory roles to assess therapeutic potential.MethodsWe identified CCL family expression profile utilizing ONCOMINE, and their relationship with the pathological stage and Gleason Score of PCa patients. The genetic alterations and protein-protein interactions were investigated in PCa.

pmc-13183649.title: A qualitative meta-analysis on the lived experience of siblings of persons with mental illness
pmc-13183649.creator: Massimiliano Sommantico, Marina Lacatena, Jacopo Postiglione, Santa Parrello
pmc-13183649.description: Having a brother or sister with mental illness (MI) has a profound effect on well-siblings’ health, quality of life, and relationships, and there is relatively little knowledge about their needs for information and support. The article presents a qualitative meta-analysis examining the lived experience of well-siblings of persons with MI.

(b) Reimbursement of research, development, and maintenance costs (1) Research and development payment (A) In.
